Scripture. God inspired the human authors of the Bible's 66 books, so God is its author. It is true in all it says and the highest standard for every belief and practice. All of it points to Christ.

God. One living and true God, holy, all-knowing, all-powerful, Creator and Ruler of all, eternally Father, Son and Holy Spirit: three persons, one God. The Father rules creation and history in wisdom and grace, and is Father to all who become His children through faith in Christ. The Son, Jesus Christ, is eternally God. Conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, He is fully God and fully man and never sinned. He died in the place of sinners, rose bodily, ascended, and is the one mediator between God and people. He will return in glory to judge the world. The Holy Spirit is fully God. He inspired Scripture, convicts of sin, draws people to Christ and gives new birth. He lives in every believer from conversion, seals them for the day of redemption, gives gifts to serve the church, and makes believers like Christ.

Humanity. God made man and woman in His image, equal in worth; being male and female is part of His good creation. Through Adam's choice sin entered the world. Everyone inherits a nature inclined to sin and becomes a sinner once able to choose. Only grace restores us. People of every race have full dignity.

Salvation. Offered freely to all who receive Jesus as Lord and Savior, who bought it with His blood; there is no salvation apart from personal faith in Him. It includes regeneration (new birth by the Spirit, answered by repentance and faith), justification (God declares sinners righteous by grace through faith, not works), sanctification (lifelong growth in holiness) and glorification (the final, perfect state of the redeemed).

God's purpose of grace. Election is God's gracious purpose to save sinners, consistent with human freedom and responsibility, leaving no room for boasting. True believers persevere to the end: they may fall into sin and suffer for it, but God keeps them and they will not lose their salvation.

The church. A local church is a self-governing congregation of baptized believers, joined by covenant, keeping the two ordinances and spreading the gospel, governed democratically under Christ. Its officers are pastors (also called elders or overseers) and deacons. Men and women are both gifted for service, but the office of pastor is limited to men as Scripture qualifies them. The church is also the body of Christ: all the redeemed of every age and nation.

Baptism and the Lord's Supper. Baptism is a believer's immersion in water in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, picturing Christ's death, burial and resurrection, the believer's new life, and the coming resurrection. It does not save; it is obedience after salvation and comes before church membership and the Supper. The Lord's Supper is a symbolic act: members share the bread and cup to remember Christ's death and await His return.

Last things. Jesus will return personally and visibly, in God's time; the dead will be raised and Christ will judge everyone. The unrighteous go to hell, everlasting punishment; the righteous live forever with the Lord in glorified bodies. The confession does not settle the millennium or the order of end-time events.

Evangelism and missions. Every Christian and church must make disciples of all nations, by word and life.
Education. Faith and learning belong together; Christian schools have real freedom, bounded by Christ's preeminence and the Bible's authority.
Stewardship. Time, talents and possessions belong to God; Christians give gladly, regularly and generously.

Cooperation. Churches may join associations and conventions for missions; these have no authority over churches. Christians may work with other Christians without compromising loyalty to Christ and His Word.

The Christian and society. Christ is Lord of all of life. Christians oppose racism, greed and all sexual immorality, including adultery, homosexuality and pornography; care for orphans, the poor, the abused, the elderly and the sick; and defend human life from conception to natural death, always in love and without compromising truth.

Peace and war. Christians seek peace with all; the true answer to war is the gospel.

Religious liberty. God alone is Lord of the conscience. Church and state are separate: the state protects every faith's freedom and favors none, and faith must never be forced. Christians pray for and honor rulers, but obey God first.

The family. Marriage is the lifelong covenant of one man and one woman. Husband and wife are equal in worth; the husband leads, protects and provides with servant love, and the wife graciously submits to that leadership and helps him. Children are a blessing from conception; parents teach them God's ways, and children honor and obey them.
